chunks: 2316 - And he, peace be upon him, said:
“Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sanctified Makkah
‘on the day He created the heavens and the earth,’

its vegetation is not to be cut, its trees are not to be lopped, its game is not to be disturbed, and its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who announces it. Then al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib stood before him and said: O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, except al-Idhkhir, for it is for the grave and for the roofs of our houses. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله remained silent for a moment, and al-ʿAbbās regretted what he had said. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Except al-Idhkhir.’”

key_terms.الْإِذْخِرُ: a type of grass permitted as an exception
key_terms.لِمُنْشِدٍ: for one who publicly announces and seeks the owner

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the sanctity of Makkah and the exception of al-Idhkhir?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sanctity of Makkah and mentions legal restrictions within its sacred precinct, including prohibitions on cutting vegetation, harming trees, disturbing game, and taking lost property except for public announcement. It also records the exception of al-Idhkhir, which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم permitted due to practical need.
